svg.title: Query Execution Plans
svg.desc: Query Execution Plans. Read EXPLAIN the way the planner thinks: scans, joins, estimated against actual rows, and the statistics behind each choice. Step 1, The report is slow: The country report takes 106 ms to return 6 rows, and the team starts guessing at the cause. Step 2, Reading the plan: Read from the leaves up: 48 rows expected, 23,213 found, so 23,213 index lookups and 93% of buffers. Step 3, Estimates versus reality: Histogram ends 2 Sep, so the planner guessed 48 rows. After ANALYZE: a hash join and 6,198 buffers. Step 4, Pitfalls in production: EXPLAIN alone only estimates; ANALYZE runs it. Generic plans can't see $1. Log slow plans in prod.

g.text: The country report takes 106 ms to return 6 rows, and the team starts guessing at the cause.
Read from the leaves up: 48 rows expected, 23,213 found, so 23,213 index lookups and 93% of buffers.
Histogram ends 2 Sep, so the planner guessed 48 rows. After ANALYZE: a hash join and 6,198 buffers.
EXPLAIN alone only estimates; ANALYZE runs it. Generic plans can't see $1. Log slow plans in prod.
plans the query, then runs the plan
Which plan? How many rows? Where did the time go?
Most expensive: 23,213 index lookups, 93% of all buffers
They happen because the scan was estimated at 48 rows: for 48,
a Nested Loop looked cheapest (cost 11,409 vs 14,408 hash join).
cost: planner units, not ms; a node includes its children
Hash Join: 6,198 buffers instead of 74,704 · 106 → 88 ms
With 22,956 rows expected, one pass over customers into a hash
is cheapest: cost 14,928 vs 22,701 for a nested loop.
warm cache here: every page was already in memory
Seq Scan on orders o (rows=166,667): a third of the table,
because a generic plan cannot see the value of $1.
PostgreSQL kept custom plans here: the generic one cost more
Add an index on every column?
None of them looks at what the
operation, then the index it reads
ms to first row..last row, per loop
8 kB pages; hit = already in memory
then follow the time and the buffers.
